serous acinar cell.description: Serous acinar cells of submucosal glands in the airways, producing antimicrobial proteins and serous fluid.

mucous acinar cell.description: Mucous acinar cells of submucosal glands, secreting heavily glycosylated mucins and immunomodulatory peptides.

goblet cell.description: Airway goblet cells, mucus-secreting epithelial cells lining the bronchial lumen.

club cell.description: Club cells are non-ciliated secretory cells of the bronchioles, secreting proteins and detoxifying xenobiotics.

basal cell.description: Basal cells are quiescent airway epithelial stem cells that anchor to the basement membrane and give rise to secretory and ciliated lineages.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: A lung fibroblast subtype located in the alveolar interstitium, characterized by expression of FGF7 and COL13A1, and involved in alveolar homeostasis.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: A lung fibroblast subtype associated with the adventitia of blood vessels and airways, marked by PI16 and FGF10 expression.

Myofibroblast.description: A contractile fibroblast with alpha-smooth muscle actin expression, involved in wound healing and fibrosis.

Pericyte.description: A perivascular cell attached to the basement membrane of capillaries, expressing RGS5 and MCAM, crucial for vascular stability.

Smooth muscle cell.description: A contractile cell of the airway and vascular walls, expressing MYH11 and DES.

Alveolar Resident Macrophage.description: Resident alveolar macrophages are self-renewing, tissue-resident phagocytes that maintain lung homeostasis and surfactant catabolism.

Interstitial Macrophage.description: Interstitial macrophages reside in the lung interstitium and are involved in tissue remodeling, antigen presentation, and immunomodulation.

Monocyte-derived Alveolar Macrophage.description: Monocyte-derived alveolar macrophages are recruited to the lung during infection or injury and display a pro-inflammatory, immunomodulatory phenotype.

Conventional Dendritic Cell.description: Conventional dendritic cells are professional antigen-presenting cells that migrate to lymph nodes to activate naive T cells and can be confused with macrophages in lung tissue.

Monocyte.description: Monocytes are circulating precursors of tissue macrophages and dendritic cells, often contaminating lung tissue preparations and confused with alveolar macrophages.

Mature Alveolar Type 1 (AT1) Cells.description: Mature alveolar type 1 cells are squamous epithelial cells that line the alveoli and mediate gas exchange, expressing AGER, AQP5, CLIC5, and other AT1-specific markers while lacking surfactant and fibroblast markers.

Transitional AT1/AT2 Cells.description: Transitional AT1/AT2 cells are an intermediate epithelial population observed during lung injury and repair, co-expressing AT1 (AGER, AQP5) and AT2 (SFTPC, LAMP3) markers and enriched for KRT8 and stress-associated genes.

Alveolar Type 2 (AT2) Cells.description: Alveolar type 2 cells are cuboidal surfactant-secreting epithelial stem/progenitor cells that express SFTPC and other surfactant proteins, plus LAMP3 and ABCA3, and are distinct from AT1 cells and fibroblasts.

Alveolar Fibroblasts.description: Alveolar fibroblasts are interstitial cells expressing collagen and ECM genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, PDGFRA, DCN) that provide structural support and regulate alveolar remodeling.

Adventitial Fibroblasts.description: Adventitial fibroblasts are perivascular interstitial cells surrounding larger vessels and airways, expressing collagens, PDGFRA, PI16, and ADAM33, distinct from alveolar AT1/AT2 epithelial cells.

Naive B cells.description: Mature antigen-inexperienced B lymphocytes expressing high surface IgM and IgD, enriched for markers of resting follicular B cells.

Memory B cells.description: Long-lived antigen-experienced B cells that rapidly differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells upon rechallenge.

Plasma cells.description: Terminally differentiated antibody-secreting cells expressing high levels of immunoglobulin genes and ER stress-related proteins.

T cells.description: Cytotoxic or helper T lymphocytes characterized by the expression of the CD3 complex and T cell receptor genes.

Alveolar macrophages.description: Tissue-resident macrophages lining the alveolar space with high expression of scavenger receptors and genes for lipid metabolism.

MUC5AC-high goblet cell.description: Airway goblet cell subtype producing MUC5AC mucin, enriched in proximal airways and associated with type 2 inflammation.

MUC5B-high goblet cell.description: Airway goblet cell subtype producing MUC5B mucin, enriched in distal airways and submucosal glands, maintaining airway homeostasis.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory cells that produce club cell secretory protein and detoxify inhaled xenobiotics.

Ciliated cell.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells that propel mucus via coordinated ciliary beating, with high expression of ciliary motor proteins.

Basal cell.description: Undifferentiated airway epithelial progenitor cells expressing high levels of p63 and keratins, anchoring to the basement membrane.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: Fibroblast subset located in the adventitial layer around airways and vessels, expressing extracellular matrix remodeling genes and Pi16/DPT.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Fibroblast subset associated with alveolar septa, expressing SFRP4 and COL13A1, involved in alveolar structure maintenance.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblast phenotype expressing smooth muscle actin and collagen, often associated with fibrosis and wound healing.

Airway smooth muscle cell.description: Smooth muscle cell wrapped around bronchial airways, expressing muscle contraction genes and specific markers such as MYH11 and SMTN; frequently confused with fibroblasts in single-cell annotations.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cell associated with capillaries and venules, expressing PDGFRB and RGS5; a distinct mesenchymal cell type that can be confused with fibroblasts.

Chemosensory brush cell.description: Rare chemosensory epithelial cells in lung airways that detect microbial and irritant stimuli via taste-like signaling, producing IL-25 and prostaglandins to regulate immunity.

Cholinergic brush cell.description: A subtype of lung brush cell that synthesizes acetylcholine, potentially signaling to nerve fibers and immune cells via paracrine mechanisms.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: Innervated epithelial cells that act as oxygen sensors and secrete neuropeptides like CGRP and bombesin, often confused with brush cells due to their rarity and dense-core granules.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting epithelial cells that produce mucins and trefoil factors, playing a central role in airway defense and often overrepresented in chronic lung disease.

General capillary endothelial cell (gCap.description: The predominant capillary endothelial subtype in lung parenchyma, supporting gas exchange and vascular integrity.

Aerocyte capillary endothelial cell (aCa.description: A specialized capillary endothelial subtype with high carbonic anhydrase 4 expression, involved in gas exchange and immune surveillance.

Lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Lung lymphatic endothelial cells lining lymphatic vessels, regulating fluid balance and immune cell trafficking.

Pulmonary venous endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining pulmonary veins that carry oxygenated blood from capillaries back to the heart.

Pulmonary arterial endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining pulmonary arteries that deliver deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lung capillaries.

cDC2.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells expressing CD1c and high levels of MHC class II, specialized in CD4+ T cell priming.

DC3.description: CD1c+ CD14+ dendritic cells with monocyte-like features, potent in inflammatory responses.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages in the lung that clear surfactant and pathogens, expressing high levels of PPARG and MARCO.

Plasmacytoid DC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells specialized in type I interferon production, expressing IL3RA and CLEC4C.

Classical monocyte.description: Circulating monocytes with high CD14 expression, precursors of macrophages and dendritic cells.

Th1.description: CD4+ T helper type 1 cells that produce interferon-gamma and support cellular immunity against intracellular pathogens.

Th17.description: CD4+ T helper 17 cells producing IL-17A/F and IL-22, involved in mucosal immunity and neutrophil recruitment at barrier sites.

Treg.description: CD4+ regulatory T cells that suppress immune responses and maintain self-tolerance and tissue homeostasis.

CD8+ T.description: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes that kill infected and malignant cells via perforin and granzyme release.

NK cell.description: Natural killer cells providing innate cytotoxic defense against tumors and virally infected cells without prior sensitization.

CD8+ Tissue-resident memory T cell (TRM).description: Tissue-resident memory CD8+ T cells that persist in lung parenchyma, expressing adhesion and residency markers like ITGAE/CD103 and CD69, and are poised for rapid local recall responses.

CD8+ Central memory T cell (TCM).description: Central memory CD8+ T cells with lymph node homing capacity via CCR7 and CD62L, expressing stemness-related transcription factors TCF7 and LEF1, and displaying high proliferative potential.

CD8+ Effector memory T cell (TEM).description: Effector memory CD8+ T cells that circulate through blood and tissues, expressing cytotoxic molecules (GZMB, PRF1) and killer cell lectin-like receptors, adapted for immediate effector function.

CD4+ Th1 cell.description: CD4+ T helper 1 cells characterized by expression of master regulator TBX21 (T-bet) and production of IFN-gamma, promoting cell-mediated immunity against intracellular pathogens.

Natural killer (NK) cell.description: Innate lymphoid natural killer cells that exhibit cytotoxic activity without prior sensitization, expressing a repertoire of killer cell lectin-like receptors and cytolytic granule components.

Classical monocytes (CD14+).description: CD14+ classical monocytes with high inflammatory cytokine production and myeloid cell differentiation potential.

Non-classical monocytes (CD16+).description: CD16+ patrolling monocytes that survey endothelium and produce anti-inflammatory cytokines.

Intermediate monocytes (CD14+CD16+).description: Transitional CD14+CD16+ monocytes with both inflammatory and antigen-presenting functions.

Alveolar macrophages.description: Tissue-resident macrophages in lung alveoli involved in surfactant clearance and immune regulation.

Conventional dendritic cells type 2 (cDC.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells specialized in CD4 T cell priming and Th2/Th17 responses.

Club cell (canonical).description: Mature SCGB1A1+ club cells, the primary secretory cells of bronchioles, producing surfactant proteins and detoxifying xenobiotics.

Club cell (transitional/KRT8+).description: KRT8+ transitional club cells representing an intermediate state during airway repair, co-expressing club cell and injury markers.

Goblet cell.description: MUC5AC/MUC5B-secreting goblet cells of the airway epithelium, involved in mucus production and innate defense.

Ciliated cell.description: FOXJ1+ ciliated cells with motile cilia that facilitate mucociliary clearance in the airway lumen.

Alveolar type 2 cell.description: Surfactant-producing cuboidal alveolar epithelial cells that serve as progenitors for AT1 cells and maintain alveolar homeostasis.

cDC1.description: Conventional dendritic cell type 1, specialized in antigen cross-presentation to CD8 T cells.

cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cell type 2, specialized in CD4 T cell activation and humoral immunity.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cell, primary producer of type I interferons upon viral infection.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophage in the alveolar space, involved in surfactant clearance and immune surveillance.

Monocyte-derived DC.description: Infiltration monocyte-derived dendritic cell appearing during inflammation, with a mixed monocyte/DC phenotype.

cDC1.description: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells specialized in CD8+ T cell cross-presentation, marked by CLEC9A, XCR1, and CADM1.

cDC2.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells that promote CD4+ T cell responses and express high levels of CD1C, FCER1A, and CLEC10A.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells specialized in type I interferon production, expressing LILRA4, CLEC4C, and IRF7.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident alveolar macrophages that maintain lung homeostasis and surfactant clearance, marked by MARCO, FABP4, and MRC1.

Classical monocyte.description: Classical CD14+ monocytes that circulate and migrate to tissues, expressing FCN1, S100A8/9, and CD14; commonly confused with dendritic cells in lung parenchyma.

M1-like elicited macrophage.description: Elicited macrophage in a pro-inflammatory, classically activated (M1) state, highly expressing inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and pattern recognition receptors.

M2-like elicited macrophage.description: Elicited macrophage in a pro-resolving, alternatively activated (M2) state, expressing genes for tissue repair, anti-inflammatory mediators, and scavenger receptors.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Resident alveolar macrophage of the lung, characterized by high expression of scavenger receptors and lipid metabolism genes essential for surfactant catabolism and immune surveillance.

Classical monocyte.description: Classical CD14+ peripheral blood monocyte, a precursor of elicited macrophages, highly expressing S100 alarmins and LPS co-receptor CD14.

Lymphatic endothelial cell (quiescent).description: Resting lymphatic endothelial cells lining lung lymphatic vessels, characterized by high expression of PROX1, PDPN, and LYVE1.

Lymphatic endothelial cell (proliferatin.description: Actively dividing lymphatic endothelial cells expressing cell-cycle markers on top of core LEC identity.

Blood vascular endothelial cell (BEC).description: Vascular (blood) endothelial cells, well-represented in lung, often confused with lymphatic endothelium but expressing KDR and CLDN5 instead of PROX1 and LYVE1.

Alveolar type 1 (AT1) cell.description: Extremely thin alveolar epithelial type I cells covering gas-exchange surface; share PDPN expression with lymphatic endothelial cells, leading to mutual misannotation.

Alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells.description: Thin squamous alveolar epithelial cells lining the gas-exchange surface, marked by AGER and PDPN.

Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells.description: Cuboidal alveolar epithelial cells responsible for surfactant production and secretion, marked by SFTPC and NAPSA.

Club (Clara) cells.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar epithelial cells that secrete immunomodulatory factors and detoxify inhaled xenobiotics, marked by SCGB1A1 and CYP2F1.

Pulmonary alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages in the alveolar airspace that clear surfactant and pathogens, marked by MARCO and FABP1.

Lung endothelial cells.description: Vascular endothelial cells forming lung capillaries and vessels, marked by PECAM1 and VWF.

Alveolar lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-associated fibroblast in the alveolar interstitium that supports alveolar epithelial cells and participates in lipid metabolism and surfactant homeostasis.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: Fibroblast located in the adventitia of airways and blood vessels, contributing to extracellular matrix organization and perivascular niche regulation.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile and matrix-producing fibroblast that becomes prominent during injury and fibrosis, expressing alpha-smooth muscle actin and extracellular matrix genes.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cell lining airways and vasculature, characterized by smooth muscle myosin heavy chain and other contractile apparatus genes.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cell that wraps around capillaries and venules, expressing RGS5 and PDGFRB, and regulates microvascular tone and permeability.

Long-term hematopoietic stem cell.description: Quiescent, self-renewing stem cells at the apex of the blood hierarchy, rare but detectable in lung vascular niches.

Short-term hematopoietic stem cell.description: Multipotent cells with limited self-renewal and increased proliferative activity, giving rise to all blood lineages.

Multipotent progenitor.description: Committed progenitors with multilineage potential but no self-renewal, showing early myeloid/lymphoid priming.

Lung endothelial cell.description: Cells lining pulmonary blood vessels, expressing CD34 and PECAM1, frequently misannotated as HSCs due to shared CD34 expression.

Lung mast cell.description: Granular immune effector cells expressing KIT and tryptases, commonly mistaken for hematopoietic progenitors because of high KIT and CD34 expression.

CFTR-high ionocyte.description: A rare pulmonary epithelial cell subtype characterized by high CFTR expression and FOXI1/ASCL3 transcription factors, mediating chloride secretion and airway surface liquid homeostasis.

V-ATPase-high ionocyte.description: A rare pulmonary epithelial cell subtype with elevated vacuolar ATPase subunits and FOXI1, contributing to acid-base regulation and proton secretion.

Tuft cell.description: A rare chemosensory epithelial cell in the airway, expressing TRPM5, POU2F3, and DCLK1, involved in type 2 immune responses.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: A rare innervated airway epithelial cell that secretes peptides like CGRP, expressing ASCL1, CHGA, and SYP.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident alveolar macrophages that line the airspaces and are specialized for surfactant catabolism, phagocytosis, and immune regulation; high expression of PPARG and C1Q family.

Interstitial macrophage.description: Interstitial macrophages residing in the lung parenchyma adjacent to airways and vessels; involved in antigen presentation, tissue remodeling, and immunomodulation via LYVE1 and FOLR2.

Monocyte-derived macrophage.description: Monocyte-derived macrophages recruited from blood during inflammation; characterized by pro-inflammatory and tissue-remodeling gene expression, including S100A8/9 and CCR2.

Conventional dendritic cell.description: Conventional dendritic cells (cDC1 and cDC2) that sample antigens and present peptides to T cells; distinguished by expression of CD1C, CLEC9A, and high MHC class II.

Mature pericyte.description: Classic lung pericyte expressing contractile and pericyte surface markers, surrounding capillaries and regulating microvascular tone.

Activated pericyte.description: Pericyte subset that acquires myofibroblast-like extracellular matrix and inflammatory gene expression during tissue remodeling.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Vascular smooth muscle cell with abundant contractile filaments, often confused with pericytes due to shared expression of ACTA2 and TAGLN.

Fibroblast.description: Interstitial fibroblast producing collagens and matrix proteins, commonly confused with pericytes because both express PDGFRB and matrix remodeling genes.

Mast cells (MCT type).description: Mucosal mast cells that express mainly tryptase and are associated with lung airway epithelium and type 2 immune responses.

Mast cells (MCTC type).description: Connective-tissue mast cells that co-express tryptase and chymase, typically found adjacent to blood vessels and within the submucosa.

Basophils.description: Circulating granulocytes that are frequently confused with mast cells due to shared expression of Fc receptors; distinguished by the absence of tryptase/chymase.

Eosinophils.description: Granulocytes involved in allergic inflammation that share granular markers; distinguished by expression of EPX, RNASEs, and SIGLEC8.

Mesothelial cells (canonical).description: Resting pleural mesothelial cells lining the lung surface, characterized by expression of classic mesothelial markers MSLN, WT1, and CALB2.

Activated mesothelial cells (EMT).description: Mesothelial cells undergoing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, with loss of apical-basal polarity and acquisition of migratory, pro-fibrotic properties.

Fibroblasts.description: Subpleural fibroblasts, often confused with mesothelial cells due to shared expression of VIM and SPARC, but distinguished by robust collagen and PDGFRA expression.

Smooth muscle cells.description: Vascular or airway smooth muscle cells in lung parenchyma, characterized by contractile machinery genes, and a potential confound due to ACTA2/TAGLN expression in activated mesothelial cells.

Alveolar type 1 cells.description: Alveolar type 1 pneumocytes covering the gas-exchange surface, sharing expression of PDPN with mesothelial cells but distinguished by AQP5, AGER, and CLIC5.

MUC5AC-high goblet cells.description: Airway surface goblet cells with high MUC5AC expression, representing the classical mucus-secreting cell of the proximal lung.

MUC5B-high goblet cells.description: Peripheral airway goblet cells preferentially expressing MUC5B, common in distal lung parenchyma and associated with submucosal gland-like differentiation.

Club cells.description: Bronchiolar club cells that secrete SCGB proteins and are commonly confused with mucus-secreting cells due to their abundance in distal airways.

Ciliated cells.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells with motile cilia, a common neighboring cell type in the airway epithelium that can be misannotated as goblet cells.

Basal cells.description: Airway basal cells that serve as progenitor cells and are morphologically distinct but sometimes confused with secretory goblet cells in single-cell data.

Proximal multiciliated columnar cell.description: Multiciliated columnar cells lining the proximal tracheobronchial airways, enriched for motile cilia structural genes and low secretory gene expression.

Distal multiciliated columnar cell.description: Multiciliated cells in bronchiolar epithelium with residual secretory features, co-expressing cilia genes and club cell markers such as SCGB1A1.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated, secretory club cells of the bronchiolar epithelium, often confused with ciliated cells due to colocalization; high expression of secretoglobins and cytochrome P450 enzymes.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting goblet cells of the airway epithelium, characterized by gel-forming mucins and mucus processing genes.

Alveolar type 2 cell.description: Alveolar type 2 epithelial cells responsible for surfactant production; can be confused with airway cells in parenchymal samples.

Mature ciliated cell.description: Multiciliated epithelial cells lining conducting airways that beat to propel mucus; express FOXJ1 and axonemal dyneins.

Deuterosomal cell.description: Transit-amplifying progenitors undergoing centriole amplification for multiciliogenesis; express CCNO and DEUP1.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cells that produce club cell secretoglobins and xenobiotic metabolism enzymes in distal airways.

Goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting epithelial cells producing gel-forming mucins and responsible for airway mucus plugging in disease.

Basal cell.description: Undifferentiated airway progenitor cells attached to basement membrane that can self-renew and differentiate into ciliated and secretory cells.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile matrix-producing cells in lung parenchyma characterized by expression of ACTA2 and TAGLN, contributing to tissue remodeling.

Pathogenic myofibroblast.description: Activated myofibroblast state associated with pulmonary fibrosis, marked by CTHRC1 and SPP1 and enhanced extracellular matrix production.

Smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile cells of the airway and vascular walls expressing MYH11 and CNN1, distinct from myofibroblasts by higher levels of muscle-specific contractile proteins.

Pericyte.description: Perivascular cells surrounding capillaries with strong PDGFRB and RGS5 expression, often confused with myofibroblasts due to overlapping contractile markers.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-containing fibroblastic cells with TCF21 and LPL expression that support alveolar epithelium and can be confused with myofibroblasts based on PDGFRA positivity.

MUC5AC-high goblet cells.description: Airway goblet cells characterized by high MUC5AC expression, involved in mucin production and secretion.

MUC5B-high goblet cells.description: Distal airway goblet cells enriched in MUC5B expression, contributing to mucous and antimicrobial defense.

Club cells.description: Non-ciliated columnar epithelial cells that secrete Clara cell proteins and detoxify xenobiotics, often confused with goblet cells due to secretory morphology.

Ciliated cells.description: Multiciliated airway epithelial cells with motile cilia, frequently misannotated as goblet cells in noisy scRNA-seq data.

Basal cells.description: Stem/progenitor cells of the airway epithelium, often confused with goblet cells in basaloid/metaplastic states.

Conventional NK cells (CD56dim).description: Cytotoxic CD56dim natural killer cells with high expression of perforin and granzymes, circulating and patrolling in lung parenchyma.

Tissue-resident NK cells (trNK).description: Resident natural killer cells in lung parenchyma expressing CD69, CXCR6, and integrins, specialized in tissue surveillance and local immune responses.

Adaptive NK cells (NKG2C+).description: Adaptive NK cells with high expression of NKG2C and KIRs, expanded during viral infections and mediating antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.

CD8+ T cells (confused).description: CD8+ T cells, including effector and memory subsets, that share cytotoxic molecules with NK cells and are commonly confused in single-cell annotations.

ILC1s (confused).description: Group 1 innate lymphoid cells that are non-cytotoxic tissue-resident cells, sharing surface markers and transcription factors with NK cells but distinct in development and function.

Non-classical monocyte (patrolling).description: CX3CR1hi CD16+ patrolling non-classical monocytes that adhere to and survey the vasculature and extravasate into lung tissue.

Non-classical monocyte (MHCIIhi).description: MHCII-expressing, activated non-classical monocytes with increased antigen-presentation and interferon-stimulated gene expression, found in inflamed lung parenchyma.

Classical monocyte.description: CD14hi CD16- classical monocytes with pro-inflammatory and antimicrobial functions, a major precursor for lung macrophages and a common confound with CD16+ cells.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident alveolar macrophages expressing high levels of PPARG, MARCO, and C1Q, foam-like cells in the airway lumen that are frequently confused with non-classical monocytes due to autofluorescence.

Conventional dendritic cell type 2 (cDC2.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells with robust antigen-presentation machinery and CD1c/FCER1A expression, resident in lung interstitium and a key differential diagnosis for CD16+ monocyte-derived cells.

IgA plasma cell.description: IgA-secreting plasma cells enriched in lung mucosa, marked by expression of immunoglobulin alpha heavy chain and plasma cell transcriptional regulators such as PRDM1 and IRF4, with high secretory machinery genes.

IgG plasma cell.description: IgG-secreting plasma cells in lung parenchyma, marked by expression of immunoglobulin gamma heavy chain genes and strong antibody secretion machinery, often associated with systemic immune responses.

Plasmablast.description: Proliferating antibody-secreting cells transitioning from activated B cells to plasma cells, characterized by high expression of cell cycle genes and plasma cell markers.

Memory B cell.description: Antigen-experienced quiescent B cells that can differentiate into plasma cells upon reactivation, classically marked by CD27 and CD20, and often confused with plasma cells in lung.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Type I interferon-producing dendritic cells with plasma cell-like morphology, expressing markers such as LILRA4 and CLEC4C, and often mistaken for plasma cells in single-cell annotations.

pDC (quiescent).description: Core plasmacytoid dendritic cell cluster characterized by high expression of CLEC4C, LILRA4, and IRF7, reflecting the resting IFN-producing state.

pDC (activated).description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cell cluster with strong type I interferon response and costimulatory molecule upregulation, indicating viral infection or TLR activation.

cDC1 (conventional dendritic cell type 1.description: Conventional dendritic cell type 1 subset expressing CLEC9A and XCR1, specialized in cross-presentation to CD8 T cells.

cDC2 (conventional dendritic cell type 2.description: Conventional dendritic cell type 2 cluster marked by CD1C and FCER1A, specialized in CD4 T cell presentation.

Monocyte.description: Classical monocytes with high S100A8/9 and CD14, often confused with dendritic cells due to overlapping expression of HLA-DR and myeloid markers.

Alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells.description: Alveolar type 1 (AT1) epithelial cells are extremely thin, squamous cells that cover ~95% of the alveolar surface and mediate gas exchange; they express specific markers such as AGER and HOPX.

Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells.description: Alveolar type 2 (AT2) epithelial cells are cuboidal, surfactant-secreting cells that also serve as alveolar progenitors; they express SFTPC and ABCA3.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Alveolar macrophages are resident immune cells within the alveolar space that perform phagocytosis and express CD68, MARCO, and C1Q.

Lung capillary endothelial cell.description: Lung capillary endothelial cells line the dense network of capillaries in the alveolar interstitium and facilitate gas exchange by transporting O2 and CO2; they express PECAM1, VWF, and CA4.

pulmonary alveolar type 1 cell.description: Thin squamous alveolar epithelial cells covering the alveolar surface and facilitating gas exchange; identified by AGER, PDPN, and CLIC5 expression.

pulmonary alveolar type 2 cell.description: Cuboidal alveolar epithelial cells that secrete surfactant and act as progenitors for AT1 cells; identified by SFTPCs, LAMP3, and NAPSA.

alveolar macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages in the alveolar space that clear surfactant and pathogens; identified by APOE, C1Q genes, and MARCO.

lung capillary endothelial cell.description: Endothelial cells lining alveolar capillaries forming the air-blood barrier; identified by CA4, VWF, and PECAM1.

AT2 mature.description: Classical pulmonary alveolar type 2 cells expressing high levels of surfactant proteins and lipid metabolism genes, responsible for surfactant production and alveolar homeostasis.

AT2 proliferative.description: Proliferative pulmonary alveolar type 2 cells with elevated expression of cell cycle and DNA replication genes while retaining AT2 identity through surfactant protein expression.

AT1.description: Pulmonary alveolar type 1 cells, extremely thin squamous epithelial cells expressing genes for gas exchange, ion transport, and endothelial-like features.

Club cell.description: Club (Clara) cells, non-ciliated bronchiolar epithelial cells with secretory and xenobiotic metabolism functions, expressing secretoglobin genes.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Alveolar macrophages, tissue-resident immune cells in the lung alveoli with high expression of phagocytosis, lipid metabolism, and inflammatory mediators.

pulmonary artery endothelial cell (condu.description: Cells lining the lumen of large pulmonary arteries, characterized by high expression of arterial specification genes such as HEY1, GJA5, and SEMA3G, and Notch signaling components.

pulmonary arteriole endothelial cell (sm.description: Cells lining smaller intrapulmonary arteries and arterioles, distinguished by higher expression of CXCL12 and matrix-associated genes, representing a transition to the capillary bed.

pulmonary capillary endothelial cell.description: Cells lining the alveolar capillaries, responsible for gas exchange and expressing high levels of CA4 and EDNRB, with a distinct molecular profile from arterial and venous endothelium.

pulmonary venous endothelial cell.description: Cells lining pulmonary veins, characterized by expression of NR2F2, VWA1, and ACKR1, and often confused with arterial endothelium due to shared pan-endothelial markers.

pulmonary lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Cells lining lymphatic vessels in the lung, defined by expression of PROX1, FLT4, and PDPN, and distinct from blood vascular endothelium.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell (PNEC).description: Pulmonary neuroendocrine cells are rare airway epithelial cells with neurosecretory granules, marked by ASCL1 and dense-core granule proteins, and involved in chemosensation and hormone release.

Tuft cell (brush cell).description: Tuft cells are rare chemosensory epithelial cells with microvilli, expressing cholinergic signaling and eicosanoid mediators, often confused with neuroendocrine cells due to their scarcity and epithelial location.

Pulmonary ionocyte.description: Pulmonary ionocytes are rare airway epithelial cells specialized for ion transport, marked by FOXI1 and CFTR expression, and can be mistakenly annotated as neuroendocrine cells in single-cell analyses.

Respiratory basal cell (classical).description: Classical airway basal stem/progenitor cells lining the respiratory bronchioles, marked by high TP63 and KRT5 expression, providing regenerative capacity.

Respiratory basal cell (secretory-differ.description: Transitional basal cells with a mixed basal/secretory phenotype, representing the initial step toward club cell differentiation in small airways.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory club cells in the bronchiolar epithelium, frequently confused with basal cells due to co-expression of certain airway genes.

Alveolar type II (AT2) cell.description: Cuboidal alveolar epithelial type II cells that produce surfactant and act as progenitors for AT1 cells; a common distal lung neighbor that may be misannotated as respiratory basal.

KRT13+ hillock cell.description: Canonical KRT13+ hillock cell, a rare airway epithelial subtype with squamous differentiation potential.

S100A7+ squamous-differentiating hillock.description: S100A7+ squamous-differentiating hillock population with enhanced cornification gene expression.

Basal cell.description: Airway basal stem/progenitor cell expressing TP63 and basal keratins, often confused with hillock cells.

Suprabasal cell.description: Intermediate airway epithelial cell between basal and differentiated layers, marked by KRT6/KRT17.

Airway smooth muscle.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells that encircle the bronchial tree and regulate airway tone; often distinguished by expression of SLIT3, TGFBR2/TGFBR3, and MME.

Vascular smooth muscle.description: Smooth muscle cells surrounding pulmonary arteries and veins that control vascular tone; marked by PLN, GUCY1A1, PRKG1, and elastin-associated genes.

Myofibroblast.description: Activated fibroblasts with contractile properties, expressing alpha-SMA and ECM genes such as COL1A1 and POSTN, commonly confused with smooth muscle due to overlapping TAGLN and ACTA2 expression.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells that wrap around capillaries and post-capillary venules, marked by RGS5, PDGFRB, NOTCH3, and NDUFA4L2, often confused with smooth muscle due to low-level expression of contractile genes.

Fibroblast.description: Resident interstitial cells that produce extracellular matrix components such as collagens and proteoglycans, distinguished from smooth muscle by expression of PDGFRA, CD34, and absence of MYH11 and CNN1.

Alveolar Fibroblast.description: Mesenchymal cells in the alveolar interstitium that support alveolar structure and lipid metabolism, marked by LPL and GPC3.

Adventitial Fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts surrounding large vessels and airways that contribute to extracellular matrix organization, marked by PI16 and DPT.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile fibroblasts that express smooth muscle actins and are involved in wound healing and fibrosis.

Alveolar Type II Cell.description: Epithelial cells that secrete surfactant and serve as alveolar progenitors, marked by SFTPC and ABCA3.

Endothelial Cell.description: Vascular lining cells expressing CD31 and VEGFR2, forming the lung vasculature.

CD4+ T cells.description: CD4+ helper T cells that coordinate immune responses via cytokine secretion and activation of other immune cells, commonly present in lung parenchyma.

CD8+ T cells.description: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that kill infected or malignant cells through granzyme/perforin and cytokine production, enriched in lung parenchyma.

Regulatory T cells.description: Immunosuppressive regulatory T cells expressing FOXP3 and CTLA4 that maintain peripheral tolerance and modulate lung inflammation.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells that provide rapid innate immunity and are frequently misannotated as T cells due to shared markers and cytotoxic granules.

Tissue-resident memory T cells.description: Tissue-resident memory T cells that persist in lung parenchyma and provide rapid local immunity upon re-encounter with antigens.

Tracheobronchial goblet cell.description: Mucus-secreting goblet cell lining the proximal tracheobronchial airways, characterized by high expression of MUC5AC and MUC5B.

Bronchiolar goblet cell.description: Distal airway goblet cell subtype with MUC5B dominance and expression of club-like markers, found in bronchiolar epithelium.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory cell of the distal airways, often confused with goblet cells due to overlapping secretory functions and markers.

Ciliated cell.description: Multiciliated airway epithelial cell with motile cilia, a common neighboring cell type that may be misclassified as goblet cells in mixed populations.

Tracheobronchial smooth muscle (contract.description: Canonical airway smooth muscle cells in the trachea and large bronchi, characterized by high expression of contractile apparatus genes and involved in bronchoconstriction.

Tracheobronchial smooth muscle (syntheti.description: Airway smooth muscle cells in a synthetic/proliferative state, with reduced contractile protein expression and increased production of extracellular matrix, growth factors, and inflammatory mediators, often associated with airway remodeling.

Pulmonary vascular smooth muscle.description: Smooth muscle cells surrounding pulmonary arteries and veins, expressing vascular-specific genes such as gap junction proteins and potassium channels, and regulating vascular tone.

Myofibroblast.description: Activated fibroblasts with contractile properties, expressing both fibroblast markers (COL1A1, PDGFRA) and smooth muscle markers (ACTA2, TAGLN), implicated in fibrosis and tissue repair.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells wrapped around capillaries and small vessels, distinct from smooth muscle cells by high expression of RGS5, PDGFRB, and NOTCH3, supporting vascular stability and remodeling.

Pulmonary Vein Endothelial Cells.description: Endothelial cells lining pulmonary veins and large venules, marked by ACKR1 and NR2F2, regulating leukocyte trafficking and vascular tone.

Post-capillary Venule Endothelial Cells.description: Specialized venular endothelium with high expression of adhesion molecules and chemokines, facilitating immune cell extravasation in lung parenchyma.

Lymphatic Endothelial Cells.description: Endothelial cells forming lymphatic vessels, characterized by PROX1 and LYVE1, responsible for fluid homeostasis and immune cell transport.

Capillary Endothelial Cells.description: Endothelial cells of pulmonary capillaries, expressing CA4 and EDNRB, critical for gas exchange and blood flow regulation.

Arterial Endothelial Cells.description: Endothelial cells of pulmonary arteries, expressing GJA5 and EFNB2, involved in vasoconstriction and oxygen sensing.
